articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週：日曜日の試合のポイント、疑問点、ファンタジーの視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者がすべての熱戦を振り返り、日曜日に行われた各試合の最も重要な疑問に答えます。第2週から見えてきたポイントはこちらです。
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly WR Darius Cooper.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

PHI-TEN | GB-NYJ

CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI | NO-BAL

CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

Philadelphia 24, Tennessee 20

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles

How should we feel about the Eagles after this game? The offensive line was too leaky for the second straight week. The defense had issues suppressing an offense that ranked 31st in total yards (195) in Week 1. And quarterback Jalen Hurts, operating without running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) for much of the game, had two interceptions. Hurts orchestrated a touchdown drive in the final seconds to walk away with a win, but Philly's schedule is only going to get tougher from here.

What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw an interception on the Eagles' opening drive -- his first on a pass thrown into the end zone since Week 10 of 2024 -- and another in the second half. But he bounced back to calmly lead the Eagles downfield in the closing moments before finding Darius Cooper for the game winner with 14 seconds left. -- Tim McManus

Next game: at Bears (Monday, Sept. 28, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Titans

What does this loss do for the Titans' confidence going forward? On paper, this game was lopsided. But both units fed off each other. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll found a nice groove orchestrating two long scoring drives. The defense had interceptions by Amani Hooker and Marcus Harris that led to 10 points. But this is the kind of game the Titans need to find a way to win. Playing the Eagles closely could give them confidence going forward, but when will these turn into wins?

What to make of the QB performance: Ward appeared comfortable executing Daboll's offense. Both of the Titans' touchdowns came via Ward's legs, making him the fifth quarterback in franchise history with two rushing TDs in a game over the past 50 seasons. And Ward's 41-yard pass to Elic Ayomanor was the fourth longest of his career. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Atlanta Braves clinch 7th NL East title in 9 years
articles.description: Under first-year manager Walt Weiss, Atlanta has rebounded after missing the playoffs last season.
articles.headlineJa: アトランタ・ブレーブス、9年間で7度目のナ・リーグ東地区優勝を果たす
articles.descriptionJa: 就任1年目のウォルト・ワイス監督のもと、アトランタは昨季のプレーオフ逃しから見事に巻き返した。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- The Atlanta Braves clinched their seventh NL East championship in nine years on Sunday with a 4-2 win over the Houston Astros.

Mike Yastrzemski hit a three-run homer during a four-run sixth inning to give the Braves the lead. After Dylan Dodd struck out the side in the ninth to clinch the title, the team ran onto the field to celebrate with hugs and take a team photo in championship hats and T-shirts.

Under first-year manager Walt Weiss, the Braves have rebounded after missing the playoffs last season with a disappointing 76-86 record and fourth-place finish in the NL East, snapping a streak of seven straight playoff appearances that included six consecutive NL East titles from 2018 to 2023.

That run was highlighted by beating the Astros to win the 2021 World Series.

Atlanta has won 24 division titles, tying the Dodgers for the most division championships since the inception of the divisional format in 1969. Atlanta has won the NL East 19 times in 32 seasons.

The Braves clinched a postseason berth on Friday night with a 6-2 win over the Astros but had a subdued celebration, with the team having a simple toast with bubbly as their focus was set on the NL East crown.

Atlanta has the third-best record in the NL at 92-64. The top two teams in the league get a first-round bye in the playoffs.

The Braves have won at least 90 games in five of the past eight seasons. The only teams with more 90-win seasons over that span are the Dodgers, who have eight, and the Yankees, with six.

articles.headline: Playoff hopeful Blue Jays avoid series sweep with 7-2 win over AL West-leading Texas
articles.description: — Toronto leadoff hitter Brett Bateman reached base and scored three times, twice knocked in by Nathan Lukes, and the Blue Jays beat the AL West-leading Texas Rangers 7-2 on Sunday to avoid a series sweep in the matchup of playoff hopefuls.
articles.headlineJa: プレーオフ進出を狙うブルージェイズ、ア・リーグ西地区首位のテキサスに7-2で勝利しスイープを回避
articles.descriptionJa: トロントの1番打者ブレット・ベイトマンが3度出塁して3得点を記録（うち2回はネイサン・ルークスの打点）。ブルージェイズは日曜日にア・リーグ西地区首位のテキサス・レンジャーズを7-2で破り、プレーオフ進出を争うカードでの3連敗（スイープ）を免れた。
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Toronto leadoff hitter Brett Bateman reached base and scored three times, twice knocked in by Nathan Lukes, and the Blue Jays beat the AL West-leading Texas Rangers 7-2 on Sunday to avoid a series sweep in the matchup of playoff hopefuls. 


              Bateman walked twice against Texas starter Jacob deGrom (11-10), scoring on a sacrifice fly by Lukes in the first and a go-ahead RBI single by Kazuma Okamota in the fifth. Bateman had a leadoff double to ignite a four-run seventh, scoring on a single by Lukes. 


              With six games remaining, the Rangers (78-78) kept a one-game lead in the AL West after Houston (77-79) lost 4-2 at home to NL East champion Atlanta. The Astros own the division tiebreaker. 


              Toronto (77-79) had the same record as the Astros, and both were 2 1/2 games behind the Chicago White Sox for the third and final wild card. 


              Spencer Arrighetti (9-9), the second of seven Blue Jays pitchers, got the win despite giving up the only Texas runs over his two innings.


              DeGrom, who has been dealing with mild groin tightness, left with the bases loaded in the fifth and the Rangers down 3-2. Left-handed reliever Robert Garcia induced an inning-ending double-play grounder on his first pitch. 


              DeGrom allowed five hits, walked four and hit another batter. The two-time Cy Young Award winner's two strikeouts put his season total at 196, just short of his fifth career 200-strikeout season. 


              Lukes had a single and scored on Sean Keys' double in the third for a 2-0 Blue Jays lead. Texas got even on Jake Burger's 27th homer, a two-run shot in the fourth that went 398 feet and deflected off Bateman's extended glove when he leaped at the wall in center field. 


              Up next
              Toronto opens a three-game series in Baltimore on Monday night. The Rangers have a day off before opening their final home series Tuesday night against the New York Mets.


              ------

articles.headline: Yastrzemski hits a 3-run homer and the Braves clinch the NL East title with 4-2 win over the Astros
articles.description: — Mike Yastrzemski hit a three-run homer during a four-run sixth inning and the Atlanta Braves clinched the NL East title for the seventh time in nine years with a 4-2 win over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ヤストレムスキーが3ラン放つ、ブレーブスがアストロズに4-2で勝利しナ・リーグ東地区優勝を確定
articles.descriptionJa: 6回に4点を奪う攻撃の中でマイク・ヤストレムスキーが3ラン本塁打を放ち、アトランタ・ブレーブスは日曜日にヒューストン・アストロズを4-2で下して、過去9年間で7度目となるナ・リーグ東地区優勝を決めた。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Mike Yastrzemski hit a three-run homer during a four-run sixth inning and the Atlanta Braves clinched the NL East title for the seventh time in nine years with a 4-2 win over the Houston Astros on Sunday.


              Ozzie Albies tied it at one with an RBI single before Yastrzemski’s homer to right off Bryan King (3-6).


              After finishing 76-86 and missing the playoffs last season, Atlanta bounced back this year under first-year manager Walt Weiss. The Braves are 92-64 and have won at least 90 games for the fifth time in the last eight seasons.


              The Astros’ playoff hopes took a hit after being swept by the Braves. Houston, which has lost seven of its last nine games, trails the Rangers by a game in the AL West, but the Astros own the tiebreaker. The Rangers lost 7-2 to Toronto on Sunday.


              Jose Altuve had a home run in the fourth, Yainer Diaz hit a home run in the eighth, but the Astros left the bases loaded in the first and fifth innings.


              Victor Mederos (5-1) entered with the bases loaded and one out in the fifth and struck out Altuve before inducing a groundout by Diaz to end the inning. Dylan Dodd pitched the ninth for his second save.


              Braves starter Martín Pérez allowed one run on six hits in 4 1/3 innings.


              Houston starter Hunter Brown scattered three hits and struck out 10 over five scoreless innings.


              Up next
              Braves: RHP JR Ritchie (1-3, 5.03 ERA) starts Tuesday in the first game of a three-game series against the Reds at home.


              Astros: RHP Cristian Javier (2-6, 5.31) starts Tuesday against the Mariners in the first game of a two-game series in Seattle.

articles.headline: Falcons' Drake London gets into verbal confrontation with fan
articles.description: Falcons wide receiver Drake London got into a verbal confrontation with someone in the crowd during his team's 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ファルコンズのドレイク・ロンドン、観客と口論に
articles.descriptionJa: ファルコンズのワイドレシーバー、ドレイク・ロンドンは、チームがパンサーズに34-3で大敗した日曜日の試合中、観客席の人物と口論になった。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- Falcons wide receiver Drake London got into a verbal confrontation with someone in the crowd during his team's 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

Cameras on the sideline picked up London appearing to lob profanities at an unknown person with teammate Olamide Zaccheaus holding him back. London said "personal stuff" was said to him, and he reacted but knows "it's not the right thing to do."

"I'm going to be honest here, I don't take light to disrespect at all," London said. "I don't care who you are. I'm a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it's not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations."

London had four catches for 51 yards as the Falcons' offense continued its struggles. Quarterback Cooper Rush had two interceptions and a lost fumble before being benched for undrafted rookie Jack Strand in the third quarter. Atlanta is still awaiting the return of Michael Penix Jr. (left ACL) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique).

"I think we as playmakers -- us in the backfield, us on the outside, on the wing -- we got to go out there and make plays regardless," London said. "We're all in the league for a reason, right? We're all good football players. I don't care if you're fourth string or you're the starter."

London admitted the score of the game did factor into how he reacted with the person in the crowd. When asked if it was a fan, London just said, "It was somebody."

"But with how the game was going and what was said to me, I don't like it," London said.

London signed a four-year, $141 million contract extension with the Falcons in the offseason, which will keep him in Atlanta through the 2030 season.

articles.headline: Christian Pulisic starts, gets first Milan goal of 2026 in win
articles.description: AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: クリスチャン・プリシッチが先発、勝利を収めた試合で2026年初のミランでのゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランは日曜日、サン・シーロでレッチェに3-0で勝利し、セリエAでの無敗記録を伸ばしました。
articles.body:
AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.

Christian Pulisic fired Ruben Amorim's side ahead early on before second-half goals from Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira wrapped up the win.

Milan now go into the international break fifth in the standings thanks to their third win of the campaign alongside two draws.

Lecce looked to strike in the opening stages as Joel Monteiro and Ivan Ilic both went close, but Milan took the lead in the 14th minute through Pulisic.

A brilliant piece of skill saw the United States striker coolly bring down Strahinja Pavlovic's cross-field pass with a single touch before moving the ball onto his left foot and firing into the bottom corner.

The goal was Pulisic's first for Milan of the calendar year after his red-hot start to the 2025 campaign came to a screeching halt in 2026. The U.S. star was not selected by Mauricio Pochettino for the squad that will play four friendlies in the upcoming international window.

Mike Maignan was called into action to make the save from Kialonda Gaspar, and before the break Milan went close in quick succession as Koni De Winter nodded wide before Pavlovic's effort was stopped by Wladimiro Falcone.

Pervis Estupiñán had a shot blocked after the restart, but Milan doubled their advantage 61 minutes in through Rabiot, who completed a team goal following a quick exchange with Gonçalo Ramos before slotting the ball past Falcone.

Estupinan fired wide as the hosts looked to build on their lead, and just moments later Moreira scored their third goal of the evening.

The substitute won the ball just inside Lecce's half and raced down the left flank before cutting into the box, where he evaded the visiting defense and hit a low finish underneath Falcone in the 73rd minute.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headlineJa: チャージャーズのTEデビッド・ニョーク、膝の負傷で負傷退場
articles.descriptionJa: チャージャーズのタイトエンド（TE）デビッド・ニョークは、日曜日のレイダース戦の第2クォーターで右膝を負傷し、医療用カートに乗せられて退場しました。
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku exited Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter on a medical cart with an injury to his right knee.

The Chargers officially listed Njoku as questionable to return.

Njoku appeared to get injured while blocking for running back Omarion Hampton. The entire team came out on the field to give Njoku well wishes as he exited.

It wasn't the only Chargers injury on the day, as safety Derwin James exited the game in the first quarter with a hand injury. In his absence, the Chargers allowed a 40-yard touchdown to wide receiver Tre Tucker. The Chargers said James was questionable to return.

The Chargers signed Njoku to a one-year deal in May after he spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns.

With Njoku out, the Chargers will lean on tight ends Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. Patrick Herbert, a practice squad player who is the brother of quarterback Justin Herbert, could also see time if Njoku's injury is long term.

Njoku had six receptions for 67 yards through two games with the Chargers.
